+# ALYQ Cloud POS — Storefront V2 Phase 1 final report
+
+**Date:** 24 September 2026\
+**Status:** Phase 1 implemented and validated as an **opt-in public presentation**. Phase 2 has not started.\
+**Open:** `#/store/v2` · `#/store/v2/products` · `#/store/v2/products/:slug-or-id`
+
+## Delivery and architecture
+
+1. **Scope.** V2 is a new, original, minimal, mobile-first storefront presentation, not a replacement commerce system. It reads the existing published shop data and leaves checkout/order authority in the existing implementation.
+2. **Public routing.** Added V2 home, catalogue and product detail under `#/store/v2/*` inside the public `/store` branch; unknown V2 subpaths return to the V2 home. No staff authentication is required just to browse.
+3. **Legacy coexistence.** `#/store`, `#/store/products`, existing product deep links, cart, checkout, account, about, contact and tracking still use their existing routes and pages. V2-to-legacy cart navigation and legacy catalogue navigation were exercised.
+4. **Provider reuse.** V2 mounts within the same `StorefrontProvider`, `StoreAccountProvider` and `StoreCartProvider`; the route chooses a V2 shell instead of `StoreLayout`, without a second cart, session or catalogue state machine.
+5. **Data and service reuse.** Product/category/variant data comes through `StorefrontProvider` and `src/modules/storefront/data/storefrontCatalog.ts`; website content, orders and settings continue through `src/modules/online/data/` and the existing services/RPC contracts.
+6. **Back-office and database boundary.** No V2 work changed POS/Admin behavior, inventory mutation, reservation logic, order placement, SQL, RLS or schema, and nothing was deployed. Existing unrelated dirty worktree changes—including pre-existing database files—were preserved, not reset or incorporated into this V2 implementation.
+7. **Implementation map.** `src/App.tsx` registers routes; `src/modules/online/StorefrontApp.tsx` selects the shell; `src/modules/online/v2/` contains the shell, pages, product card, variant chooser, appearance/price/variant adapters, primitives and scoped CSS. Paired EN/AR strings are in `src/lib/i18n/dictionary.ts`.
+
+## Shopper experience
+
+8. **Design tokens.** `.store-v2` scopes layout, typography, spacing, colors, button/card shapes and responsive rules. The appearance adapter reads saved website settings and supplies contrast-aware foreground colors; it does not apply V2 tokens to POS/Admin.
+9. **Languages and direction.** Existing i18n drives English LTR and Arabic RTL, including headings, labels, currency formatting, navigation, selection controls and footer. The language switch does not change a selected product's identity.
+10. **Announcement bar.** Existing enabled messages, configured colors, links and timed *rotate* mode feed a compact announcement. A separate scrolling ticker animation is not implemented; see point 33.
+11. **Header.** Responsive, centered brand/wordmark, configured search/account/cart entries, live cart count, desktop navigation and language control are present. Optional header controls respect saved enablement flags.
+12. **Keyboard navigation and mobile drawer.** The skip link focuses the main content without changing the HashRouter route. A labelled drawer provides shop/category/info links and language switching; it traps keyboard focus, closes on Escape, restores focus/body scrolling and keeps its long navigation independently scrollable.
+13. **Search.** Header search and the catalogue form use V2 catalogue query URLs; direct query-string/category/offer links can be opened without going through the home page.
+14. **Homepage configuration.** Existing saved section order, visibility, titles, limits, links and imagery drive the homepage. Sections with no qualifying configured content are omitted; an all-empty configuration receives an intentional empty state.
+15. **Hero.** Configured desktop/mobile slide imagery, titles, CTAs, overlay, content placement and heights are used. Multiple slides have controls and timed advance that pauses on interaction/reduced motion; no V2-specific stock photography or copied reference-site assets were added.
+16. **Editorial modules.** Configured categories, campaigns, promo banners, lookbook/editorial/text-image/about, trust strip, newsletter, brands, reviews, FAQ, social gallery and contact sections render only when their relevant existing data is available.
+17. **Merchandising modules.** Featured, best sellers, new arrivals, curated collection and sale sections derive from published products, actual sale history/selection and live offers; they do not fabricate a best-seller ranking, product or promotion.
+18. **Product grid.** The catalogue and merchandising grids show two columns on the requested mobile widths, three at tablet and four by default on desktop. Saved desktop column count and card gap can override the desktop presentation.
+19. **Product cards.** Cards share one reusable component with actual imagery, localized name/brand, advisory price, configured badges, availability, swatches, wishlist and Quick Add/options. Saved image aspect/fit, text alignment and visibility controls are applied.
+20. **Wishlist and Quick Add.** Wishlist delegates to the existing account provider. Simple products can use Quick Add; products with more than one exact published variant open an explicit option chooser instead of guessing a combination.
+21. **Catalogue controls.** Search, category/brand, stock/offer and price controls, sort order and URL state use the existing catalogue query. V2 price range and price sorting additionally use the same advisory promotion-aware price shown on its product cards.
+22. **Product detail.** PDP includes breadcrumbs, real product/content media and thumbnails, localized descriptions, SKU, price, availability, quantity, configured content/specifications, reviews and related items. Missing media uses a labelled fallback; unpublished size-guide content is not invented.
+23. **Exact variant identity.** Color and size choices come from active published variant rows, not an inferred color×size grid. Numeric sizes including `16.5`, saved letter labels such as `XS` and `One Size`, and combined color+size choices retain the selected variant UUID.
+24. **Availability and selection.** Sold-out combinations remain visible but disabled; a color change clears the old size selection. Reserved quantities are reflected when available to the client; tracking-disabled and unsellable products cannot be Quick Added. Neither the UI nor the cart silently substitutes a different variant.
+25. **Advisory price.** Variant overrides, live campaigns and promotions appear on cards/PDP and in V2 price filtering/sorting. These browser values are advisory; the existing server-side `place_online_order` flow still checks current stock, coupons and final price.
+26. **Cart/order handoff.** V2 adds `{product_id, variant_id, quantity}` through the existing cart provider. Separate exact shelves stay separate cart lines; V2 does not decrement inventory directly, bypass reservations, create an alternate checkout or place orders itself.
+27. **Footer.** Settings-backed brand description, social links, shop/information links, contact details, policy links, copyright and language switch are responsive in EN/AR. The newsletter CTA opens email; it is **not** an unimplemented subscription endpoint.
+28. **States and preview SEO.** Loading, empty, retryable data-error, unavailable and not-found states are provided. V2 sets `noindex, nofollow` while it is an opt-in preview rather than the canonical shop; its metadata is cleaned up on leaving the route.
+
+## Validation and outcome
+
+29. **Static/build checks.** `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` passed; `npm run lint` passed with **0 errors, 34 warnings** in the worktree. `git diff --check` passed. No warning was misreported as an error-free lint run.
+30. **Logic and DOM E2E.** `npm run test` passed **46/46 logic suites**, including **7/7 focused V2 logic tests**. The full `npm run test:e2e` passed **22/22 suites**; after the skip-link fix the focused V2 E2E reran and passed **28 DOM checks** for data, routing, EN/AR, keyboard focus, sold-out options, exact UUID cart lines, override pricing and legacy handoff. jsdom is not treated as visual proof.
+31. **Real-browser V2 acceptance.** Chromium checked home, catalogue and PDP at **320, 360, 375, 390, 414, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920 px**, in both **EN/LTR and AR/RTL**: **60/60** page cases. Additional fixture-based exact-variant PDP checks passed **20/20** language/width cases, with expanded card chooser samples in both languages at 320, 390, 768, 1440 and 1920 px. Tests checked header actions/centering, the keyboard skip link's focus and unchanged route, mobile drawer fit/scroll/Escape/body unlock, loaded images, visible control bounds, grid columns, headings, footer reachability, horizontally scrollable category chips, absence of page overflow and browser console/network errors. A persisted palette, five desktop columns, square imagery and hidden card controls/section were verified after reload. Representative screenshots were inspected and live in ignored `coverage/visual-v2/` during the test session.
+32. **Legacy/POS/Admin assurance.** The separate rendered acceptance suite passed **80 screens**, including legacy storefront, Admin pages/theme reloading and EN/AR POS layout/scrolling at crowded desktop and tablet sizes. The full logic/E2E suites also cover existing POS, Admin and online flows. These checks found no regression attributable to V2; they are not a claim of exhaustive production coverage.
+
+## Boundaries and next approval
+
+33. **Known Phase 1 limitations.** V2 is intentionally opt-in, not the canonical `/store` route; checkout/account/about/contact/tracking remain legacy pages. A universal size chart is not manufactured when product size information is absent. The announcement's existing `scroll` mode displays a message without a scrolling ticker. Newsletter actions use `mailto:` only. Browser tests used the isolated demo catalogue plus test-only variants, not a live production Supabase deployment; no formal accessibility certification or production-order test is claimed.
+34. **Future settings support / stop point.** `appearance.ts` already exposes typed, *non-persisted* override hooks for a mobile logo, header/footer/button/badge/border/hero colors, text, logo height and sticky header. A future, explicitly approved phase can add admin persistence/preview for those controls, consider ticker parity and decide whether to move other shopper pages to V2. None of that work, any database migration, or **Phase 2** was started here.

+# ALYQ Cloud POS — Storefront V2 Phase 2 final report
+
+**Date:** 24 September 2026\
+**Status:** Phase 2 implemented and validated locally; Phase 3 **not started**.\
+**Admin:** `#/online/website?tab=v2` (requires `manage_website`)\
+**Public opt-in preview:** `#/store/v2` · `#/store/v2/products` · `#/store/v2/products/:slug-or-id`\
+**Scope:** Presentation and website settings only. Legacy `#/store` remains the default storefront.
+
+## Architecture and ownership
+
+1. **Outcome.** A bilingual V2 Customization Studio now edits a typed, persisted V2-only appearance group inside the existing Website Admin. Saved changes affect the opt-in V2 shell; they do not launch another CMS or change checkout, POS, stock or order authority.
+2. **Repository hygiene.** Existing dirty tracked and untracked work was inspected and preserved. No clean/reset/revert, unrelated overwrite, deployment, push, pull request or GitHub operation was performed. The pre-existing untracked SQL migration is unrelated and was not touched.
+3. **Entry and authorization.** The existing website-management route adds a **STOREFRONT V2** tab. It remains behind the page's existing `manage_website` permission; a cashier cannot open the editor. Public V2 browsing remains unauthenticated.
+4. **Single settings document.** The new `WebsiteSettings.storefront_v2` type is a presentation-only group with nullable/inherit defaults. The existing `website_settings` JSONB row, demo localStorage repository, atomic `saveSettings` path, draft/saved state, Save/Discard actions, invalidation notification and media uploader are reused.
+5. **Migration decision.** Read-only inspection of the latest identified `website_settings_guard()` in `supabase/migrations/0047_admin_danger_zone.sql` found no top-level JSON key whitelist. This additive, backwards-compatible group does **not** require a migration. No SQL, RLS, RPC or Edge Function was changed.
+6. **Read and write safety.** `resolveSettings` fills old documents with V2 defaults and repairs the new group on reads. `sanitizeSettings` rebuilds it from an explicit allowlist on saves; the V2 appearance adapter sanitizes again at rendering. The old SQL guard validates its existing shared fields but **does not** server-validate V2-only keys; the client/rendering boundary is intentional and documented, not presented as a new database guarantee.
+7. **Shared versus V2-only ownership.** Shared brand, logos, hero slides, announcement content/mode, cards, badges, footer content, links and the base palette remain in their original Admin tabs. Studio shortcuts lead to those editors instead of copying them. Scope badges distinguish **Legacy + V2** from **V2 only**; background-image, legacy header preset and dark-mode switch exceptions are explicitly labelled **Legacy only**.
+8. **Routing and data boundary.** V2 still reads the existing storefront providers and catalogue. `#/store`, its legacy pages, cart, checkout, account, tracking, about and contact are unchanged. V2's new controls only supply scoped presentation tokens and header visibility; the mobile menu retains a route to the existing cart/account even if a header icon is hidden.
+
+## Customization Studio
+
+9. **Draft workflow.** Editing any V2 field updates the existing website draft, not the published shop. One Save validates the whole draft, sanitizes and persists one document; a mistyped V2 hex blocks the entire write rather than silently replacing the last valid colour. Discard still restores the last saved document.
+10. **Branding source.** The desktop V2 logo uses the existing shared logo and alternate dark-surface logo; name/wordmark falls back to shared brand values. No V2-only copy of the brand or upload pipeline was created.
+11. **Mobile logo and sizes.** An optional V2 phone logo uses `SettingsImageField` and the existing media/URL upload path; clearing it inherits the shared logo. Separate V2-only desktop and phone logo heights are constrained to 20–96px and 20–64px respectively, and the header grows to fit them.
+12. **Header presentation.** V2-only header background and text/icon colours are persisted. Sticky position, search/account/cart header icons can inherit shared visibility or use explicit V2 on/off choices; the V2 language switch can be hidden without changing the saved language or legacy storefront.
+13. **Page palette.** V2-only overrides cover page background, card surface, main text, muted text, accent and border; unset fields inherit the shared theme or a safe V2 default. Tokens are installed on `.store-v2`, not the document or Admin/POS root.
+14. **Buttons.** Background, foreground and rounded/pill/square shape are editable just for V2. Shape inherits the shared button style until overridden; the primary controls, including product actions, consume the scoped tokens.
+15. **Badges.** Background, text and square/pill shape can be overridden in V2; whether a badge appears still comes from existing card/badge/product data. No fabricated offer or badge eligibility was introduced.
+16. **Hero.** V2 has fallback background/text colours for image-free slides. It continues to use shared slides, desktop/mobile images, titles, links and placement. Image-backed slides enforce a minimum 58% dark scrim so white copy does not disappear when the shared overlay setting is too light; this guard applies only to V2.
+17. **Announcements.** Shared visibility, bilingual messages, links, static/rotate/scroll mode and interval remain the source of truth. V2-only bar/background text colours inherit these settings until overridden. Links still pass the existing safe-route adapter.
+18. **Scrolling ticker and motion.** V2 `scroll` mode now animates a seamless LTR/RTL two-copy ticker at the shared, clamped cadence. The duplicate is aria-hidden and non-interactive; animation pauses on hover or keyboard focus. With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, animation stops, the duplicate disappears and **all** configured messages remain readable in a wrapped static layout. Timed rotation also stops under reduced motion.
+19. **Footer.** Background, text and link colours have V2-only overrides. Brand description, newsletter behaviour, social/contact/policy links and copyright remain shared and still use safe destinations; no newsletter endpoint was invented.
+20. **Typography.** Body and display selectors offer curated, locally available stacks only, with Arabic serif/sans fallbacks. No free-form font family, CSS injection, arbitrary web-font URL or external font request is accepted. Arabic RTL headings/body use corresponding readable fallback stacks.
+21. **Mobile grid parity.** Below 640px, V2 now honours a V2-only one/two-column choice or inherits the shared `product_card.mobile_columns`, safely capped at 2 if a legacy setting is 3. Tablet still uses three; desktop consumes the existing shared desktop column count and card-gap controls.
+22. **Colour input and contrast.** Each V2 override has a colour picker, editable validated hex field, an inherited-value hint and a per-field Clear action. Only opaque `#RGB`/`#RRGGBB` is accepted for V2 overrides; transparent values cannot undermine contrast calculations. Effective foregrounds are checked against their actual background (including card surfaces, hero, buttons, badges, header, announcement and footer) and fall back to accessible ink at **≥4.5:1**. The Studio shows effective pair ratios and flags auto-adjustment without destroying the editable saved request.
+23. **Media and CSS safety.** The same `safeImageField` URL policy validates a V2 mobile logo; the existing remote-save converter promotes only bundled `/brand/…` media to the storefront origin. Unsupported enums, unsafe URLs, unknown JSON keys, out-of-range sizes and invalid CSS colour values are discarded on reads/saves/render; raw user CSS is not supported.
+24. **Preview honesty.** The new Admin V2 draft appearance sample uses the same adapter/CSS tokens, real shared hero and published catalogue images, and EN/AR plus phone/desktop switches. It is inert, representative and clearly labelled **not the full responsive store**; the pre-existing legacy fragment is separately labelled **not V2**. An **Open saved V2 site** link opens the actual route, with a same-tab fallback, and warns that unsaved draft changes will not appear there.
+25. **Safe reset.** A two-step **Reset V2 appearance** action replaces only `storefront_v2` in the draft with its defaults. It does not delete shared content, uploaded files, legacy styling or any commerce data; Save is still required. Per-colour Clear restores inheritance without resetting the other overrides.
+26. **Localization and keyboard use.** Studio labels, scope guidance, warnings and preview instructions are paired in EN/AR. New fields have programmatic labels, invalid state/alerts are exposed, the preview is an inert labelled group, and the public ticker respects focus and reduced-motion preferences. The existing skip link, RTL layout and mobile drawer continue to work.
+
+## Verification and limits
+
+27. **Static/production checks.** `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `git diff --check` passed. `npm run lint` passed with **0 errors and 34 existing worktree warnings**; targeted lint for the touched V2/Admin/settings files passed with no output. No warnings were represented as an entirely warning-free lint run.
+28. **Logic and DOM regressions.** `npm run test` passed **46/46 suites**, including **10/10 focused V2 logic tests** covering old JSON, allowlisting, URL conversion, mobile columns, contrasts and legacy-theme isolation. Selected `npm run test:e2e` passed **11/11 suites** covering legacy store/checkout/POS, existing website editor/theme, Admin/navigation/branding, V2 Phase 1 and the new Phase 2 Studio (**21 assertions**, plus a separate fresh-process reload). Each suite uses its own demo state.
+29. **Real-browser V2 matrix.** The earlier Phase 1 Chromium baseline passed **60/60** home/catalogue/PDP cases and **20/20** exact-variant cases. The new Phase 2 suite covered the same ten widths (320, 360, 375, 390, 414, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920px) in EN/LTR and AR/RTL and passed **40/40** configured home/catalogue cases, **20/20** configured exact-variant PDP cases and **10/10** two-column phone checks. It verified saved Admin changes after browser reload, ticker direction/focus/reduced motion, logo bounds, grid columns, absence of horizontal overflow and no browser console/network errors. Admin draft preview fit 320/390/768/1440px and switched desktop/Arabic independently. Ignored screenshots live in `coverage/visual-v2-phase2/` during this session.
+30. **Saved-state proof.** In both jsdom (fresh process) and Chromium (real reload), a saved V2 background, header, logo, shape, font and grid reached the opt-in route. The same saved document retained shared announcement/card/theme values. V2 reset was saved and verified to restore only the V2 group. Legacy `#/store` and POS still lacked V2 tokens; no alternate cart or inventory path was exercised or added.
+31. **Honest limitations.** The manual/browser runs used **demo-mode persistence**, not a production Supabase account; the Supabase save converter was unit-checked and the SQL guard inspected read-only, but a live production upsert was not attempted. Direct SQL writers bypassing the client can store malformed V2 keys; V2's renderer rejects them, but the old server guard itself does not enforce the new group. The draft sample is appearance-only and cannot reproduce full-site responsive behaviour or commerce; use **Open saved V2 site** after Save for that. This is not an exhaustive accessibility certification or production-order test.
+32. **Stop point.** Phase 2 is complete locally. No Phase 3 page migration, canonical-route switch, cart/checkout redesign, new commerce service, database migration, deployment or GitHub publication was started. V2 remains opt-in until separately authorized work changes that boundary.

+# ALYQ Cloud POS — Storefront V2 Phase 3 final report
+
+**Date:** 24 September 2026 (Africa/Cairo)
+
+**Outcome:** Phase 3's opt-in shopper journey is implemented and validated locally. This is **not** a production launch or a claim that live Supabase checkout was exercised.
+
+**Entry:** `#/store/v2` · **Canonical/legacy entry remains:** `#/store`.
+
+## Scope and ownership
+
+1. **Phase 3 outcome.** The existing V2 home, catalogue and PDP now lead through V2 bag, checkout, confirmation, private tracking, account, About and Contact pages. This final pass corrected historical reorder orderability, partial-reorder feedback and catalogue-loading races; it did not start Phase 4.
+2. **Ten opt-in public routes.** `src/App.tsx` registers `#/store/v2`, `/products`, `/products/:key`, `/cart`, `/checkout`, `/confirmation`, `/track`, `/account`, `/about` and `/contact` beneath that prefix. `:key` accepts the existing product slug or ID. An unknown V2 subroute returns to the V2 home, not to a staff screen.
+3. **Legacy separation.** `#/store` still shows the original storefront; its existing product, cart, checkout, confirmation, tracking, account, About and Contact routes remain intact. `StorefrontApp.tsx` selects the V2 shell **only** for `/store/v2` paths. No default-route switch, redirect from legacy, or Phase 4 cutover occurred.
+4. **One set of providers.** Both shop presentations mount under the existing `StorefrontProvider → StoreAccountProvider → StoreCartProvider` tree. V2 adds presentation and client-side journey guards, not a second catalogue, cart, shopper account, coupon calculator, stock ledger or order writer.
+5. **Order authority.** Catalogue visibility, current stock/variant checks and price previews are helpful browser information. The existing `StoreCartProvider.checkout()` and online-orders repository place the order; in live mode the existing `place_online_order` contract is authoritative for accepted items, availability, zones, discounts and totals. V2 never marks a payment paid or adjusts inventory directly.
+6. **Demo versus live repositories.** The tested browser ran **demo mode** with independent localStorage-backed catalogues, orders, reservations, settings and accounts. Live mode selects the existing Supabase repositories and public storefront reads when configured. A passing local demo checkout is not proof of a production order, live policy configuration or a successfully deployed migration.
+7. **Phase 2 continuity.** V2 still consumes the shared saved website content and the Phase 2 presentation-only `storefront_v2` appearance overrides, bilingual Studio settings, social channels and safe WhatsApp links. This pass did not recreate or replace the customization Studio, ticker, product images, Admin editor or POS theme.
+8. **Implementation boundary.** Routes/shell are in `src/App.tsx`, `src/modules/online/StorefrontApp.tsx` and `src/modules/online/v2/`; bilingual strings are in `src/lib/i18n/dictionary.ts`. The focused reorder guard lives in `v2/journeyModel.ts`, while `v2/StorefrontV2Account.tsx` delegates additions to the shared cart. No Phase 3 SQL/RLS/RPC or backend service was introduced.
+
+## Shopper journey and safety
+
+9. **V2 shell and navigation.** The existing V2 header, announcement, search, account/bag links, category navigation, drawer, footer, skip link and scoped `.store-v2` styles remain consistent from browsing through the last journey page; an optional hidden header icon never removes the underlying route.
+10. **Catalogue discovery.** Search, category, colour, numeric/letter size, brand, availability, offer and sorting options use published data and URL-backed query state. Browser reload retains filters. A no-result query shows an intentional empty state rather than an invented product.
+11. **Product selection.** The PDP presents published product content, actual variant rows, size guidance when configured, availability and related merchandise. Selecting Gold/17 cannot resolve to Silver/17; sold-out Gold/18 cannot be added merely because another size is available.
+12. **Real media and keyboard gallery.** The PDP uses stored images and a labelled fallback, not new stock photography. In Chromium, the size guide opened, the image lightbox announced a dialog, arrow keys moved through images and Escape returned focus to its trigger.
+13. **Bag line identity.** A cart line preserves `product_id`, the **exact** `variant_id` UUID or `null` for a simple product, and quantity. V2 shows SKU/variant detail, limits quantity to the actual shelf, and delegates add/increase/decrease/remove/clear to `StoreCartProvider`.
+14. **Current orderability.** Published and active status, current variant ownership/activity, stock tracking, on-hand stock and known reservations constrain V2 add/reorder. A tracking-disabled product is **not orderable through V2 checkout**; a `null` availability from disabled tracking is not permission to reorder it.
+15. **Persisted stale bags.** After a successful catalogue load, the shared cart removes saved lines that name missing or invalid products/variants and V2 shows a dismissible notice. It does not silently pick a replacement variant. The Chromium test seeded both a nonexistent product and wrong-product variant and observed the pruned empty bag.
+16. **Advisory totals.** Bag and checkout show the shared provider's preview of subtotal, discounts, delivery and total with a visible advisory label and loading indicator. They do not send a browser-calculated final amount as an order authority.
+17. **Coupon handling.** Applying/removing a code invokes the existing precheck; eligibility and preview are explicitly provisional. The settled DOM journey checked `WELCOME10` and a selected Cairo fee **before** placement and compared the displayed estimated total with the subsequent authoritative demo order snapshot.
+18. **Fulfilment.** Pickup and configured delivery zones share the legacy fulfilment settings. Zone selection, shipping fee, minimum-order check and address rules feed the existing checkout path; changing payment or zone does not freeze a stale order-form callback.
+19. **Contact and addresses.** Guest checkout takes name, Egyptian phone and an inline delivery address. A signed-in shopper can reuse a saved, browser-local address; checkout snapshots the actual address into the order, rather than depending on future profile edits.
+20. **Payment selection.** COD and InstaPay appear only when enabled in saved shop settings. The checkout shows the relevant instructions and does not invent another processor, proof inbox or transaction status.
+21. **Form guards.** Required name/phone, address, area, zone, minimum and stock/fulfilment availability have bilingual feedback. An empty contact cannot place an order; these front-end checks are not represented as the server's final acceptance decision.
+22. **Safe submission.** A synchronous pending guard prevents a rapid double click before React disables the button. The cart provider's existing idempotency reference and repository retain order authority; the DOM test clicked twice and observed **one** COD order, not two.
+23. **COD result.** Pickup/COD produced a real demo order number and itemized server-side snapshot through the existing order repository. Confirmation displayed the chosen Gold/17 UUID, pending order status and unpaid COD state, not a fake successful-payment claim.
+24. **InstaPay result.** The configured InstaPay option explains that staff verify payment. Its placed demo order remained `verification_required`; it was not labelled paid at checkout or after receipt.
+25. **Transfer proof.** The shared proof panel accepts a reference/image and submits through the existing repository. A successful demo upload stored proof data while payment stayed awaiting human verification. No new automatic settlement rule was added.
+26. **Confirmation truth.** Confirmation renders the returned order/lookup snapshot—reference, items/SKUs, payment/fulfilment, totals and next steps—not totals reconstructed from the current product page. The DOM and Chromium tests waited for the itemized detail, not just the first receipt heading.
+27. **Refresh and tab privacy.** A short-lived `sessionStorage` pair holds **reference + phone + timestamp**, never an order body; refresh re-queries with both. A different tab lacking the pair sees a private/track prompt, not another tab's receipt. Receipt URLs never contain the phone.
+28. **Private tracking.** A reference by itself reveals no order. The lookup requires the matching phone, keeps the phone out of the hash/query string, provides a not-found response for incorrect credentials and disables repeated submission while loading.
+29. **Status and timeline.** Correct reference + phone returns the repository's actual order status, payment status, itemized detail and workflow timeline; no browser-inferred paid, dispatched or delivered state is shown.
+30. **Browser-local shopper profile.** Registration/login, profile and persisted session reuse `StoreAccountProvider` and its local account repository in both online modes. This is intentionally **not** a Supabase Auth/staff account or a cross-device customer identity.
+31. **Addresses and wishlist.** Account tabs use the shared saved-address and wishlist actions. Guest favourites and signed-in conveniences retain their documented browser-local limits; product cards in the wishlist still read published products.
+32. **Private history.** Only references associated with the local shopper account are remembered; history entries are fetched by the existing reference-and-phone-gated repository, including after a new signed-in order or a correctly tracked guest order. The browser test waited for history loading to settle before asserting an order or a genuine empty history.
+33. **Valid reorder.** `planV2Reorder()` admits a published, active, stock-tracked simple product as a `null` variant line and an active exact variant **only under its original UUID**. It accounts for held/current cart quantities and cumulative repeated historical lines; all-valid orders continue to the V2 bag.
+34. **Refused historical lines.** Missing/unpublished/inactive products, disabled tracking, foreign/inactive/removed or sold-out exact variants, insufficient stock and malformed quantities are excluded. No same-size/sibling-colour substitution occurs; the warning identifies the old item name **and SKU**.
+35. **Partial reorder.** When an order combines valid and invalid lines, only the valid original lines are requested from the shared cart. After the cart commits, Orders shows the specific unavailable items, an EN/AR partial-success status, and an explicit V2 bag link; it stays on the warning rather than navigating away. The Chromium fixture ordered a simple product plus Gold/17, deactivated only Gold/17, and observed **only the simple item** in the bag in both languages.
+36. **Loading and state-race guard.** Order history can arrive before the catalogue. Reorder buttons now wait for the current catalogue to load (and offer retry on a catalogue error), preventing a premature false-unavailable result. React can also defer the shared cart's state updater, making `addMany()`'s immediate count temporarily zero even when it adds the line; V2 verifies the **committed** cart quantities before displaying success or a refusal.
+37. **About.** The V2 About route uses the existing bilingual `WebsiteSettings.about` title, body, image and configured CTA, with a restrained fallback for absent optional content. It does not invent a company story or separate editorial database.
+38. **Contact and social.** The V2 Contact page uses configured phone, email, address, map, hours, available zones, InstaPay link and shared social settings. Its message CTA opens a validated WhatsApp compose link if configured; otherwise it explains that no WhatsApp action is available. There is **no fictional on-site message inbox**.
+
+## Acceptance evidence
+
+39. **English/Arabic.** Shared i18n strings cover the new partial-reorder explanation in EN and AR. Chromium exercised both LTR and RTL route layouts, plus exact-SKU warnings and the bag link in both languages. Language selection never changes the persisted variant UUID.
+40. **Responsive geometry.** The rendered matrix checked **seven populated Phase 3 routes**—bag, checkout, confirmation, tracking, account, About and Contact—at **320, 360, 375, 390, 414, 430, 768, 1024, 1280, 1440 and 1920 px** in each language: **154/154 route cases**. It checked heading, V2 header actions, content bounds, document/body width and reachable footer; no case scrolled horizontally or clipped the sampled panels. Seventy representative route/language/width screenshots are Git-ignored in `coverage/visual-v2-phase3/`; four phone captures (cart, checkout, receipt, account) were visually reviewed in this pass.
+41. **Loading, empty and error states.** A fresh Chromium profile observed a labelled catalogue loading skeleton, zero-result catalogue state with working Clear filters, empty bag with Browse link, empty shopper history, required tracking-field alerts, disabled lookup while pending and private not-found alert. The DOM journey checked checkout validation and saved-cart pruning. The catalogue's retry affordance and Orders' catalogue-error retry are implemented; a production backend outage was **not** simulated.
+42. **Practical accessibility.** Chromium checked one main landmark and heading, search semantics, named inputs, product image alt text, mobile filter-dialog Escape, size-guide/lightbox focus return, status/alert roles, disabled invalid choices and no mobile overflow. V2 has a skip link, visible focus styles and Phase 2 reduced-motion handling. This is **not** an automated WCAG audit or accessibility certification; touch-target and assistive-technology coverage remain outside this test's proof.
+43. **Focused logic and DOM.** `npm test` passed **48/48 logic suites**; `journey.selftest.ts` passed **9/9** focused tests covering simple/exact reorder, unpublished/inactive/untracked/sold-out and foreign UUIDs, reserved/cart stock, duplicates, partial valid+invalid, no substitution and EN/AR keys. The current `v2-journey` DOM suite passed **29 shopper assertions** across COD, InstaPay, proof, coupons, delivery estimates, private tracking, local account and legacy isolation. Its delivery estimate was allowed to settle before comparison with the order snapshot.
+44. **Rendered, regression and static checks.** The final Chromium suite passed **154/154** route cases plus the separate PDP/filter/receipt/privacy/state/partial-reorder flows; it was repeated on the final app build and passed twice. `npm run test:e2e` passed **25/25 currently registered suites**, including older storefront, POS, Admin and Phase 1–2 regressions. `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build` and `git diff --check` passed. `npm run lint` exited successfully with **0 errors and 32 warnings across the worktree**; it was **not** warning-free, and its output listed no warning in this final pass's Phase 3 source/test files. The registered report suite uses an isolated in-memory test database; no production database action is implied by its pass.
+
+## SQL, provenance and stop line
+
+45. **Dirty SQL classification — C (attribution unprovable).** At the start of this pass `supabase/tests/scenarios.sql` was already modified and `supabase/migrations/0061_last_active_variant_guard.sql` was already untracked. Read-only inspection shows variant archive/delete permission and last-active-shelf tests; `src/modules/operations/types.ts` also refers to 0061. Local Git status, timestamps and available commit history do **not** prove who authored these uncommitted changes, so classification **A** cannot be asserted. Both SQL files remain untouched; no SQL file was applied to a project or live database, no scenario SQL was invoked directly, and no RLS/RPC edit, deployment or production DB change was performed for this pass. The registered E2E report suite's isolated in-memory SQL tests are accounted for in point 44.

Live Supabase anonymous reads/order placement, payment operations, production error recovery and formal accessibility conformance were not certified. The legacy `#/store` route, Phase 2 settings/social/WhatsApp behaviour and POS/Admin were preserved; Phase 4, canonical switch, deployment, production orders, database work and GitHub publication were **not** undertaken. Any rollout or live-schema decision needs a separate, explicit authorization and live-environment validation.

+# Storefront V2 — Phase 4A: canonical cutover and final local QA
+
+Local acceptance record · 2026-09-25 (Africa/Cairo) · branch `arena/01a0ce43-alyq-cloud-pos` · builds and browser checks in **demo mode**. This is a route/presentation cutover in the working tree, **not** a production deployment or live-payment certification. The Phase 3 baseline is `docs/STOREFRONT_V2_PHASE_3.md`; the results below were run again for this phase.
+
+## Pre-cutover decision and change boundary
+
+### 1. Phase 4A decision and scope
+The fresh pre-cutover gate passed before the canonical routes were edited, so V2 was promoted to the public `#/store` presentation. The work changes the route selection, public links, metadata, the downloadable sitemap and related tests. It does **not** start Phase 4B, change order authority, alter a database/backend, or deploy a site.
+
+### 2. Initial worktree, attribution and SQL stop line
+The checkout was already substantially dirty, including `supabase/tests/scenarios.sql` (modified) and `supabase/migrations/0061_last_active_variant_guard.sql` (untracked). Their authorship is **C — unprovable from local evidence**; neither was edited, deleted, applied, deployed or used to justify an unrelated rewrite. The tracked/untracked prior work, including Phase 1–3 V2 source, was preserved. No SQL migration, RLS/RPC, Edge Function or production database change was made for Phase 4A.
+
+### 3. Architecture preflight
+`src/App.tsx` previously mounted independent legacy canonical and V2 preview page trees. `StorefrontApp.tsx` selected its shell from the pathname but already wrapped both trees in **one** `StorefrontProvider → StoreAccountProvider → StoreCartProvider` chain. The preflight also audited configured links, V2 header/drawer/footer and social destinations, page metadata, the Admin saved-design link, route-sensitive test suites and the Phase 3 report.
+
+### 4. Pre-cutover static gate
+Before **any** route edit: `npm run typecheck` passed; `npm run build` passed (**484 modules**); `git diff --check` passed. This result belongs to the old route topology and is recorded separately from the final post-cutover build.
+
+### 5. Pre-cutover focused logic gate
+`node scripts/test.logic.mjs src/modules/online/v2` passed **3/3 suites**: journey **9/9**, V2 logic **10/10**, social safety **9/9**. The later Phase 4A route adapter adds one V2 logic assertion group; the pre-cutover **10/10** is not retroactively reported as **11/11**.
+
+### 6. Pre-cutover rendered-DOM gate
+`node scripts/test.e2e.mjs storefront-v2 v2-studio v2-social v2-journey` passed **4/4 suites** before the cutover. This included the critical exact-UUID shopper journey, COD, InstaPay proof status, private tracking, account and Admin/social flows, plus the old preview route integrity. Phase 3's historical Chromium results were background context, not substituted for this fresh gate.
+
+### 7. Gate decision and isolation rule
+Only after topics 4–6 passed was the route switch made. The cutover did not touch the cart/account provider implementations, price or stock authority, the online-order repository, payment-verification flow or POS/Admin routing. A critical regression outside routing/presentation would have stopped the switch rather than authorized a backend rewrite; none remained after final QA.
+
+## Public routing and destination audit
+
+### 8. Single canonical public route map
+One V2 route tree now owns these public destinations under `src/App.tsx`, inside the unchanged three-provider storefront boundary:
+
+| Canonical hash route | V2 presentation |
+|---|---|
+| `#/store` | home |
+| `#/store/products`, `#/store/products/:key` | catalogue; product by slug **or** ID |
+| `#/store/cart`, `#/store/checkout`, `#/store/confirmation` | bag; checkout; receipt |
+| `#/store/track`, `#/store/account` | private lookup; shopper account |
+| `#/store/about`, `#/store/contact` | merchant information and contact |
+
+There is no second V2 page tree at `v2/*`; that route has only a redirect element.
+
+### 9. Former preview-URL compatibility
+`#/store/v2` and each known former preview destination redirect with React Router `replace` to its matching canonical route. Product IDs/slugs are kept as path segments; known catalogue filters, the tracking **reference**, and an allowed account tab survive. A real Chromium back-navigation check verified the redirect does not trap the shopper in a preview loop. There is no live legacy/debug customer route.
+
+### 10. Query, identifier and privacy policy
+`canonicalStorePathname` preserves the encoded product path rather than guessing another SKU or variant. `canonicalPreviewSearch` allowlists catalogue keys (`q`, category/brand/colour/size/price/sort/availability/offer), `track?number=…` and valid `account?tab=…`; it drops other preview query fields, notably `phone` and `token`, as well as old fragment data. Configured saved preview links use the same normalization after existing URL validation. Tests cover slug/ID links, filters and the stripping of a forged tracking phone; query state is **not** payment or order authority.
+
+### 11. Unknown routes and missing products
+Unknown former-preview and unknown canonical shop paths return to `#/store` without exposing a legacy presentation. A well-formed but unpublished/unknown `#/store/products/:key` stays on a V2 not-found page, carries `noindex, nofollow`, and does not show an order. Canonical deep links, reloads and not-found behavior passed in jsdom and Chromium.
+
+### 12. Provider and backend-authority ownership
+`StorefrontApp.tsx` now renders `StorefrontV2Shell` around the same `<Outlet />` and the same provider chain. V2 cards, bag, checkout, account and private order details still delegate to shared providers/repositories; no second cart, shopper identity, pricing engine or placement path was added. The browser's calculated total and coupon preview remain advisory; the existing order placement contract remains authoritative.
+
+### 13. Retained legacy source
+`StoreLayout`, all legacy storefront pages, components, CSS and shared helpers remain physically present for rollback/regression tests. They are **not** mounted at a new customer-facing debug URL. The route/shell selection in `src/App.tsx` and `src/modules/online/StorefrontApp.tsx` is the principal rollback boundary; no destructive dead-code cleanup was performed.
+
+### 14. Normal V2 internal links
+The home CTAs, product cards, breadcrumbs, catalogue facets, PDP actions, bag/checkout/receipt/tracking/account links, mobile drawer, header, footer, information links and social-contact actions now target canonical `#/store/*` destinations. A source audit found no production V2 link still hard-coded to `#/store/v2`; the compatibility prefix remains only in the route adapter. Configured catalogue searches use the existing URL-backed parser.
+
+### 15. Stored merchant links and policies
+`v2Href()` no longer rewrites saved canonical `#/store/*` links into a preview route. It validates links through existing `configuredHref`, normalizes saved former-preview links and leaves approved external destinations alone. Unknown configured policy destinations do **not** gain invented policy pages: they retain the validated URL and otherwise follow the canonical shop's safe fallback. No merchant settings row is mutated merely by following a link.
+
+### 16. Admin public design entry
+The Admin V2 Studio's **Open saved V2** action now uses `#/store` both in its anchor and new-window/fallback behavior. The inert draft preview remains inside the Admin form and is not mislabeled as the public page; its test ID was retained to avoid breaking editor selectors. Admin save/reload/reset and permission tests were rerun; a cashier remains unable to enter the V2 editor.

+Search, category, brand, colour, numeric/letter size, prices, availability, offer and sorting remain URL-backed over the published catalogue. Former-preview URLs preserve known safe filter values, and a real browser reload retained `q`, `sort`, `color` and `size_label`. The mobile filter dialog, empty/clear state, sold-out combinations and no horizontal overflow were checked; filters do not invent stock or a variant.

+The PDP resolves either the product ID or its saved slug and publishes a canonical **slug-or-ID** metadata URL. Gold/17, sold-out Gold/18, Silver/XS and a fractional shelf were checked in isolated demo fixtures; cart/order lines preserve the chosen **variant UUID**, not an inferred colour/size substitute. Rendered gallery, size-guide, lightbox keyboard behavior, current media, price and availability were exercised in Chromium.

+V2 bag links now stay at `#/store/cart`; its lines still use the existing cart provider, product ID and exact variant UUID. Increase, decrease, remove, clear, stale-line pruning, unavailable-stock messaging, coupons and advisory delivery/total display were exercised. Nothing in the route change silently replaces an unavailable historical variant or turns a browser total into a charge.

+### 21. COD checkout and authoritative placement
+Canonical COD pickup/delivery checks covered required contact fields, saved address/zone selection, a settled advisory estimate and the existing placement repository. The order snapshot and cart retained the exact requested shelf. +The same canonical checkout offers configured InstaPay instructions and still uses the shared authoritative placement path. A jsdom journey and a separate real-Chromium journey placed an InstaPay **demo-mode** order, uploaded a proof and confirmed `payment_status === "verification_required"` after submission. Proof is evidence for a human review, **not** an automatic paid/verified claim; no payment backend was changed.

+### 23. Confirmation and receipt privacy
+`#/store/confirmation` is noindex and reads the shared placement result or a short-lived same-tab **reference-plus-phone** pair. It does not persist the full order object as a browser receipt. Chromium verified a refresh restores only the matching receipt and a different tab cannot reveal it; an empty/direct confirmation shows the private fallback.
+
+### 24. Reference-plus-phone tracking
+`#/store/track?number=…` may carry a shareable order reference but never puts the customer's phone into the URL. A blank or incorrect phone exposes no order; a correct pair reads the authoritative timeline/status through the existing lookup. Old preview tracking bookmarks strip forged `phone`/`token` query values. Tracking and its missing/error states remain noindex.

+### 25. Shopper account, wishlist, history and reorder
+The browser-local account still uses `StoreAccountProvider` for profile, addresses, wishlist and private history; an order is read by the established private lookup. Reorder accepts only currently published exact UUIDs, warns about missing/sold-out/foreign shelves and preserves a valid partial reorder without navigating away from its warning. Chromium and DOM checked sign-up/history/partial reorder in EN and AR. This is local demo evidence, not a multi-device account certification.

+### 26. About and Contact
+Configured bilingual About content, canonical About links and Contact details render in the V2 shell. Contact uses valid phone/email/map destinations and the existing WhatsApp action rather than inventing a web inbox. Both pages are public/indexable; an About CTA and Contact/social destination still pass the existing configured-link safety rules.

+### 27. Social channels and WhatsApp
+The single shared WebsiteSettings social owner governs Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and WhatsApp; invalid schemes/hosts, local-only WhatsApp numbers and disabled channels fail closed. English and Arabic prefill is URL-encoded and external links are labeled `noopener noreferrer` new-tab actions. Admin draft icons stay inert; rendered dark/light footer checks covered enabled/disabled channels and no overflow. No new social data source was added.

+### 28. Saved V2 customization
+Admin's saved V2 colours, logos, columns, media aspect, section visibility, ticker and reduced-motion behavior reached the canonical public pages after reload. The legacy theme values remain separately stored, and V2 variables are scoped to `.store-v2`, not the document or POS. Both one- and two-column mobile choices and a deliberate low-contrast palette were exercised; reset affects only the V2 draft until the existing Save action.

The existing browser-generated sitemap/robots downloads are **not hosted** `sitemap.xml`/`robots.txt` endpoints. Hash routes and client rendering are weak crawler targets: no SSR, deployed sitemap, deployed robots file or reliable search indexing is claimed.

+Rollback is a deliberate **route-level** change: restore the legacy canonical page mappings in `src/App.tsx` and legacy shell selection in `StorefrontApp.tsx`, then reconcile Admin/public-link and SEO expectations with the selected presentation. None of that work was started here; deployment, migration application and GitHub publication remain outside this completed local phase.

+# Storefront V2 — Phase 4B: dependency-audited local release candidate
+
+**Local acceptance record:** 2026-09-25 (Africa/Cairo) · branch `arena/01a0ce43-alyq-cloud-pos` · demo repositories and a locally served, built single-file app. **Not a deployment, live-order test, payment certification, database migration, or claim of reliable crawler indexing.** Phase 3 and 4A baselines: [Phase 3](STOREFRONT_V2_PHASE_3.md) and [Phase 4A](STOREFRONT_V2_PHASE_4A.md). Counts below are **fresh Phase 4B** runs unless explicitly identified as a pre-cleanup comparison.
+
+## Dependency audit and bounded cleanup
+
+### 1. Decision and scope
+Phase 4A's canonical cutover was already complete. Phase 4B audited the *current* source before cleanup, removed only proven-unused public import edges, retained test-dependent legacy source, added a repeatable dependency guard, and repeated local release-candidate validation. There was no commerce rewrite, second public route tree, debug switch, production order or deployment.
+
+### 2. Worktree preservation, provenance and SQL stop line
+The checkout started substantially dirty at `0582c5f`; tracked and untracked Phase 1–4A work was preserved. `supabase/tests/scenarios.sql` was already modified and `supabase/migrations/0061_last_active_variant_guard.sql` already untracked. Their authorship remains **C — unprovable from local evidence** (the SQL provenance classification, **not** the dead-code classification below). Neither SQL file was edited, deleted, moved, applied or deployed in Phase 4B. No migration, RLS/RPC, Edge Function, backend authority, database or staff-permission change was authorized or made.
+
+### 3. Audit method and limits
+Inspected `App.tsx`, `StorefrontApp.tsx`, the online-module barrel, all online page/component imports, dynamic/test references, rollback plugin, Admin previews, CSS entry points, i18n uses and Phase 3/4A reports. Compared esbuild **metafile input graphs** for `src/main.tsx` both with and without the ten-suite, test-only rollback projection; inspected files absent from both graphs and ran the actual registered suites. A metafile can include parsed but eventually tree-shaken files, so **absence** establishes no import edge; mere presence does not establish executed UI or bundled bytes. The runnable guard is `node scripts/storefront-v2-dependency.audit.mjs`.
+
+### 4. Classification A — canonical V2
+`src/App.tsx`'s ten public shopper destinations, `StorefrontApp.tsx`'s single provider/shell boundary, the twelve `v2/StorefrontV2*` route/shell/redirect components, V2 cards/chooser/primitives, models/appearance/route adapter and `v2/storefront-v2.css` are active. `src/modules/online/components/admin/StorefrontV2DraftPreview.tsx` also imports the V2 stylesheet for the Admin editor. Preserve all of these.
+
+### 5. Classification B — shared commerce and proof
+`StorefrontProvider`, `StoreCartProvider`, `StoreAccountProvider`, online repositories, public catalogue, pricing/promotions/coupons/zones/orders/tracking/account/media/settings/theme/SEO, `PaymentProofPanel` and `StorePrimitives` still have public or Admin dependencies. The V2 confirmation/tracking journey renders the existing proof panel (and its `FieldNote`/`Money` primitives). Cart line and order authority remain in the shared implementation; removal or parallel replacement is not cleanup.
+
+### 6. Classification B — Admin and POS dependencies
+`pages/StoreContentPage.tsx` is the authenticated content editor, **not** a retired shopper page. `WebsiteSettingsPage.tsx` still mounts both the older `StorefrontPreview` fragment and the V2 Studio/draft preview; `services/theme.ts`, shared `--store-*` tokens and `online.preview.*` translations serve those screens. The POS/Admin routes, dashboard notification/provider imports and other module-barrel exports remain required. Do not delete them on the basis of a `Store*` or `Storefront*` name.
+
+### 7. Classification B — retained legacy test dependencies
+All **ten** older shopper pages (`StoreHomePage`, `StoreProductsPage`, `StoreProductPage`, `StoreCartPage`, `StoreCheckoutPage`, `StoreConfirmationPage`, `StoreTrackPage`, `StoreAccountPage`, `StoreAboutPage`, `StoreContactPage`) are loaded by `scripts/lib/legacy-store-rollback.plugin.mjs` for **ten registered historical E2E suites**. `components/storefront/StoreLayout.tsx`, `ProductCard.tsx` and `VariantPicker.tsx` are reachable from that same projection; a branding logic test also reads five legacy files by path. They are **not** public routes after the cutover but are **not proven unused across tests/scripts**. Retained 13/13 legacy presentation modules, without a production rollback URL.
+
+### 8. Classification C — actually proven unused
+After routing the test harness to direct file imports, the **ten legacy page re-exports** in the production `src/modules/online/index.ts` barrel had no consumer. Removed those ten re-export *edges*, not their source files or behavior. The old `StoreLayout`-resident **export location** of `SocialIcon` was also unnecessary for V2 once its SVG component was moved verbatim to a small shared module. No other online production/test source file qualified: the union of both input graphs covered **every non-test `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.css` file under `src/modules/online`** in the audit. **Legacy files deleted: 0; legacy page barrel exports removed: 10.** There is no claim that test-dependent legacy files were deleted.
+
+### 9. Classification D — uncertain or not separable safely
+No CSS selector, Tailwind-generated utility, image, theme token or `store.*`/`online.*` dictionary key was removed by a guessed textual usage count. Tailwind v4 scans the source tree; dynamically assembled i18n keys and Admin/rollback dependencies make name-only deletion unsafe. There is no separate legacy CSS file: the two relevant authored stylesheets are `src/index.css` (global/shared) and `src/modules/online/v2/storefront-v2.css` (active V2/Admin). Keep D candidates until a separate per-selector/per-key proof exists; do not call them dead or claim a smaller CSS payload.
+
+### 10. Production barrel cleanup
+`src/modules/online/index.ts` now exports the active root, back-office pages and providers without re-exporting ten retired shopper pages. `src/App.tsx` still imports `StorefrontApp` and Admin/POS-related exports normally; the public route table remains untouched. This eliminates the production barrel's static path to the retired shopper page tree without removing the rollback test's source. No dynamic production import or implicit legacy URL was found.
+
+### 11. Shared SVG dependency extraction
+Moved the original five-platform `SocialIcon` implementation out of the monolithic legacy `StoreLayout.tsx` to `components/storefront/SocialIcon.tsx`. V2 shell, home and social-channel renderer import the new provider-free module; the retained legacy layout imports it too. The SVG paths, labels and social URL policy were not rewritten; the old shell is no longer imported to render V2 icons. `PaymentProofPanel`/`StorePrimitives` deliberately remain shared rather than being copied or deleted.
+
+### 12. Rollback harness after isolation
+The **test-only** esbuild plugin now imports each retained legacy page by its direct path instead of the production online barrel, then substitutes legacy routes/shell only inside a temporary jsdom bundle. Ten historical suite IDs use this rollback projection; the other **16** registered suites run the actual canonical bundle (the `store` suite additionally boots the canonical bundle for forged-social checks). This is a test architecture, **not** a shipped switch, duplicate customer route or default rollback. Any future *actual* route-level rollback would need an explicit route/shell change and link/SEO review.
+
+### 13. Repeatable graph/build evidence
+Before isolation: **470 public / 452 rollback** parsed esbuild inputs and **486** Vite-transformed modules. With the locked dependencies restored by `npm ci`: **458 public / 453 rollback** parsed inputs, **474** Vite-transformed modules. The audit asserts **13** legacy modules absent from the public graph and present in rollback, **7** shared/Admin modules and **12** canonical V2 route/shell modules present in public. +### 14. CSS, assets and presentation policy
+No legacy CSS or shared styling was removed. V2 CSS is `.store-v2`-scoped; the Admin draft also uses it. Brand/product media, fallback images, responsive utilities and `--store-*` tokens remain available to the shop, Admin fragment and proof panel. No arbitrary CSS purge, image deletion, palette change or global restyle was necessary for a truthful cleanup.

+English/Arabic dictionary entries for V2, Admin, shared order/proof/status surfaces and legacy regression were kept. Shipped page titles and configured branding still use the existing translated/content pathways.

+## Canonical routing and shopper acceptance
+
+### 16. Sole public V2 route tree
+One `#/store` V2 shell serves home; `products` and `products/:key` (published slug or ID); cart, checkout, confirmation, track, account, About and Contact. `#/store/v2/*` is a **redirect only**, with `replace`; there is no live legacy shopper tree or debug path. These routes stay outside the authenticated POS/Admin provider chain.

+### 17. Former preview-bookmark redirects
+Known former preview URLs redirect one way to their same canonical destinations. The product path segment retains the actual slug/identifier; navigation back does not loop into the preview prefix. +The public root continues to mount `StorefrontProvider → StoreAccountProvider → StoreCartProvider → StorefrontV2Shell → Outlet`. +/** TEST-ONLY projection of the retained legacy shop for rollback regression
+ * suites. The production App has *no* legacy/debug route. We compile a separate
+ * ephemeral jsdom bundle instead of changing dozens of historical DOM assertions
+ * to expect markup that no longer exists, or adding a shopper-facing escape hatch.
+ * Public V2 suites always run against the unmodified application bundle.
+ */
+import fs from "node:fs";
+import path from "node:path";
+import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
+
+const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "../..");
+const app = path.join(root, "src/App.tsx");
+const storefront = path.join(root, "src/modules/online/StorefrontApp.tsx");
+const start = "                {/* One public V2 tree; old preview bookmarks only redirect.";
+const end = '                <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/store" replace />} />';
+const legacyPages = ["StoreHomePage", "StoreProductsPage", "StoreProductPage", "StoreCartPage",
+  "StoreCheckoutPage", "StoreConfirmationPage", "StoreTrackPage", "StoreAccountPage",
+  "StoreAboutPage", "StoreContactPage"];
+const legacyPaths = ["", "products", "products/:key", "cart", "checkout", "confirmation", "track",
+  "account", "about", "contact"];
+
+function projectApp(source) {
+  const first = source.indexOf(start);
+  const last = source.indexOf(end, first);
+  if (first < 0 || last < 0) throw new Error("Legacy rollback harness: public storefront route boundary changed");
+  // Explicit direct imports keep rollback coverage without pulling the retired
+  // presentation through the production online barrel or a public URL.
+  const imports = legacyPages.map((page) =>
+    `import { ${page} } from "@/modules/online/pages/${page}";`).join("\n") + "\n";
+  const importAnchor = 'import { StorefrontV2Home } from "@/modules/online/v2/StorefrontV2Home";';
+  if (!source.includes(importAnchor)) throw new Error("Legacy rollback harness: import anchor changed");
+  const routes = legacyPaths.map((route, index) => route
+    ? `                <Route path="${route}" element={<${legacyPages[index]} />} />`
+    : `                <Route index element={<${legacyPages[index]} />} />`).join("\n") + "\n";
+  return source.slice(0, first).replace(importAnchor, imports + importAnchor) + routes + source.slice(last);
+}
+
+function projectShell(source) {
+  const oldImport = 'import { StorefrontV2Shell } from "./v2/StorefrontV2Shell";';
+  const oldOutlet = "<StorefrontV2Shell><Outlet /></StorefrontV2Shell>";
+  if (!source.includes(oldImport) || !source.includes(oldOutlet)) {
+    throw new Error("Legacy rollback harness: storefront shell boundary changed");
+  }
+  return source.replace(oldImport, 'import { StoreLayout } from "./components/storefront/StoreLayout";')
+    .replace(oldOutlet, "<StoreLayout><Outlet /></StoreLayout>");
+}
+
+export function legacyStoreRollbackPlugin() {
+  return { name: "legacy-store-rollback-test-only", setup(build) {
+    build.onLoad({ filter: /[\\/]src[\\/]App\.tsx$/ }, () => ({
+      contents: projectApp(fs.readFileSync(app, "utf8")), loader: "tsx",
+    }));
+    build.onLoad({ filter: /[\\/]src[\\/]modules[\\/]online[\\/]StorefrontApp\.tsx$/ }, () => ({
+      contents: projectShell(fs.readFileSync(storefront, "utf8")), loader: "tsx",
+    }));
+  } };
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+
+/** Prevent a false EN/AR visual pass when headless Chromium has no Arabic font.
+ * Checking DOM text, direction or document.fonts.check() does NOT prove that
+ * glyphs paint: some minimal serverless Fontconfig setups render nothing.
+ * Sample the shop's actual Arabic body font stack on a transparent canvas.
+ */
+export async function assertRenderedArabicFont(page) {
+  const ink = await page.evaluate(() => {
+    const root = document.querySelector(".store-v2");
+    if (!root || root.getAttribute("dir") !== "rtl") return 0;
+    const canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
+    canvas.width = 320;
+    canvas.height = 80;
+    const context = canvas.getContext("2d");
+    if (!context) return 0;
+    context.font = `32px ${getComputedStyle(root).fontFamily}`;
+    context.fillStyle = "#000";
+    context.fillText("مرحباً بالعالم", 4, 48);
+    const pixels = context.getImageData(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height).data;
+    let painted = 0;
+    for (let index = 3; index < pixels.length; index += 4) {
+      if (pixels[index] > 0) painted++;
+    }
+    return painted;
+  });
+  assert.ok(ink > 200,
+    `Chromium painted only ${ink} Arabic pixels: check the browser's installed fonts/Fontconfig before trusting RTL screenshots`);
+}

+/** A fresh process = a fresh browser boot, not merely a route change.
+ * The parent theme flow provides only the previously saved settings document;
+ * the demo repository and storefront provider must rehydrate it themselves.
+ */
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { createUxHarness } from "./ux-harness.mjs";
+
+const stored = process.env.ALYQ_TEST_THEME_SNAPSHOT;
+assert.ok(stored, "the prior admin session provided a saved settings document");
+const ux = await createUxHarness({ beforeImport: ({ localStorage }) => {
+  localStorage.setItem("alyq.demo.website_settings.v1", stored);
+} });
+const { dom, navigate, waitFor } = ux;
+const { document } = dom.window;
+const token = (name) => dom.window.getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue(name).trim().toLowerCase();
+await navigate("#/store", 850);
+await waitFor(() => document.querySelector("header") && token("--store-primary") === "#0f766e", {
+  label: "the newly booted public shop to load saved primary",
+});
+assert.equal(token("--store-background"), "#f1fbf6");
+assert.equal(token("--store-surface"), "#ffffff");
+assert.equal(token("--store-secondary"), "#1d3a35");
+assert.equal(token("--store-accent"), "#a18857");
+assert.equal(token("--store-text-primary"), "#183d31");
+assert.ok(document.getElementById("alyq-store-theme"), "the public provider installed the saved theme on a fresh boot");
+ux.finish("Fresh boot rehydrates the saved storefront palette");

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+/** An isolated old/forged website-settings row: the Admin rejects new bad
+ * accounts, but both public storefronts must still fail closed on old JSON. */
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
+import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
+import { DEFAULT_BUNDLE } from "./app-bundle.mjs";
+import { createUxHarness } from "./ux-harness.mjs";
+
+const snapshot = process.env.ALYQ_TEST_UNSAFE_SOCIAL;
+assert.ok(snapshot, "a fixture settings document is required");
+const ux = await createUxHarness({ beforeImport: ({ localStorage }) => {
+  localStorage.setItem("alyq.lang", "en");
+  localStorage.setItem("alyq.demo.website_settings.v1", snapshot);
+} });
+const document = ux.dom.window.document;
+const { navigate, waitFor } = ux;
+const hrefs = () => [...document.querySelectorAll("a[href]")].map((anchor) =>
+  (anchor.getAttribute("href") ?? "").trim().toLowerCase());
+const hasUnsafe = () => hrefs().some((href) => /^(?:javascript:|data:|vbscript:|#)$/.test(href));
+
+await navigate("#/store", 850);
+await waitFor(() => document.querySelector('[data-testid="product-grid"]'), { label: "fresh legacy shop" });
+assert.equal(hasUnsafe(), false, "legacy storefront never renders executable schemes");
+for (const platform of ["Facebook", "Instagram", "TikTok"]) {
+  assert.equal(Boolean(document.querySelector(`a[aria-label="${platform}"]`)), false,
+    `${platform} unsafe old settings render no icon`);
+}
+assert.equal(hrefs().some((href) => href.includes("maps.google")), false, "unsafe map link is absent");
+assert.ok(hrefs().some((href) => href.includes("wa.me/201001234567")), "valid legacy WhatsApp still works");
+
+await navigate("#/store/contact", 650);
+await waitFor(() => document.body.textContent.includes("Contact us"), { label: "fresh contact page" });
+assert.equal(hasUnsafe(), false, "legacy contact page never renders an executable or dead link");
+
+// The parent store suite uses a test-only legacy rollback bundle. Launch a
+// separate fresh boot of the *shipped* canonical app for the V2 half, rather
+// than smuggling a legacy/debug route into production.
+const publicBoot = spawnSync(process.execPath,
+  [fileURLToPath(new URL("./unsafe-social-public-reload.mjs", import.meta.url))], {
+    cwd: process.cwd(), encoding: "utf8", timeout: 60_000,
+    env: { ...process.env, ALYQ_TEST_BUNDLE: DEFAULT_BUNDLE, ALYQ_TEST_UNSAFE_SOCIAL: snapshot },
+  });
+assert.equal(publicBoot.status, 0,
+  `canonical forged-row check failed: ${publicBoot.error ?? ""}\n${publicBoot.stdout}\n${publicBoot.stderr}`);
+ux.finish("Fresh forged social settings fail closed in rollback legacy, contact and canonical V2");

+#!/usr/bin/env node
+/** Phase 4A: the shipped static build in real Chromium, exercising historical
+ * hash bookmarks, canonical reloads, metadata, keyboard escape and Admin/POS.
+ * Run with CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE and V2_VISUAL_BASE_URL against a local Vite
+ * preview; no remote backend or production deployment is involved. */
+import assert from "node:assert/strict";
+import { chromium } from "@playwright/test";
+import { assertRenderedArabicFont } from "./lib/rendered-arabic-font.mjs";
+
+const base = process.env.V2_VISUAL_BASE_URL || "http://127.0.0.1:4173";
+const browser = await chromium.launch({ executablePath: process.env.CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE || undefined,
+  args: ["--no-sandbox", "--disable-dev-shm-usage"] });
+const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 }, locale: "en-US" });
+page.setDefaultTimeout(30_000);
+const failures = [];
+page.on("pageerror", (error) => failures.push(`pageerror: ${error.message}`));
+page.on("console", (message) => { if (message.type() === "error") failures.push(`console: ${message.text()}`); });
+page.on("response", (response) => {
+  if (response.status() >= 400 && response.url().startsWith(base)) failures.push(`${response.status()} ${response.url()}`);
+});
+const go = async (hash, id) => {
+  await page.goto(`${base}/${hash}`, { timeout: 120_000 });
+  await page.getByTestId(id).waitFor({ timeout: 60_000 });
+};
+const head = () => page.evaluate(() => ({ title: document.title,
+  robots: document.querySelector('meta[name="robots"]')?.content,
+  canonical: document.querySelector('link[rel="canonical"]')?.getAttribute("href") ?? "",
+}));
+let passed = 0;
+function check(label) { console.log(`✓ ${++passed}. ${label}`); }
+
+try {
+  await go("#/store/v2", "v2-home");
+  assert.equal(new URL(page.url()).hash, "#/store");
+  assert.equal((await head()).robots, "index, follow");
+  assert.ok((await head()).canonical.endsWith("#/store"));
+  assert.equal(await page.locator('.store-v2 a[href^="#/store/v2"]').count(), 0);
+  check("old preview home replaces the hash; normal public links and indexable head are canonical");
+
+  const filters = "?q=Ring&sort=price_asc&color=gold&size_label=XS";
+  await go(`#/store/v2/products${filters}`, "v2-catalog");
+  assert.equal(new URL(page.url()).hash, `#/store/products${filters}`);
+  await page.reload();
+  await page.getByTestId("v2-catalog").waitFor();
+  assert.equal(await page.locator("#v2-search-input").inputValue(), "Ring");
+  assert.equal(new URL(page.url()).hash, `#/store/products${filters}`);
+  assert.equal((await head()).robots, "index, follow");
+  check("search, sort, colour and letter-size state survive a real redirect and reload");

+const ratio = (left, right) => {
+  const brightness = (color) => {
+    const components = color.match(/[\d.]+/g)?.slice(0, 3).map(Number);
+    assert.ok(components?.length === 3, `color ${color} is RGB`);
+    return components.map((value) => {
+      const v = value / 255;
+      return v <= 0.04045 ? v / 12.92 : ((v + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4;
+    }).reduce((sum, value, index) => sum + value * [0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722][index], 0);
+  };
+  const [a, b] = [brightness(left), brightness(right)].sort((x, y) => y - x);
+  return (a + 0.05) / (b + 0.05);
+};

+  assert.equal(reduced.duplicate, "none");
+  assert.equal(reduced.first.length, 2);
+  assert.ok(reduced.first.every((item) => item.display !== "none" && item.text));

+  console.log("✓ LTR/RTL ticker pauses on keyboard focus; reduced motion shows all messages without animation");

+    await go(`#/store/products/${variantId}`, '[data-testid="v2-product"]');
+    await page.reload();
+    await page.getByTestId("v2-color-gold").waitFor();
+    for (const width of widths) {
+      await page.setViewportSize({ width, height: width <= 414 ? 780 : 960 });
+      await page.getByTestId("v2-color-gold").click();
+      assert.equal(await page.getByTestId("v2-size-18").isDisabled(), true);
+      assert.equal(await page.getByTestId("v2-size-XS").count(), 0);
+      await page.getByTestId("v2-size-17").click();
+      assert.equal(await page.getByTestId("v2-pdp-add").isEnabled(), true);
+      await page.getByTestId("v2-color-silver").click();
+      assert.equal(await page.getByTestId("v2-pdp-add").isDisabled(), true);
+      await page.getByTestId("v2-size-XS").click();
+      assert.equal(await page.getByTestId("v2-pdp-add").isEnabled(), true);
+      assert.ok(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth + 1));
+      variants++;
+    }
+  }

+  // phone choices across EN/AR without touching the shared two-column value.
+  await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1440, height: 960 });

+  await page.reload();
+  await go("#/online/website?tab=v2", '[data-testid="v2-studio"]');

+  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Save", exact: true }).click();
+  await page.waitForFunction(() => JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem("alyq.demo.website_settings.v1"))?.settings?.storefront_v2?.mobile_columns === 2);

+        getComputedStyle(node).gridTemplateColumns.split(" ").length);

+      assert.ok(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth + 1));

+  assert.equal(await page.getByTestId("store-v2").count(), 1, "canonical catalogue uses the saved V2 design");
+  assert.equal(await page.evaluate(() => document.documentElement.style.getPropertyValue("--v2-bg")), "",
+    "V2 colours stay scoped to the storefront, not the document root");
+  await go("#/pos", '[data-testid="pos-grid"]');
+  assert.equal(await page.getByTestId("store-v2").count(), 0, "POS is not V2");
+  assert.equal(await page.locator("#alyq-store-theme").count(), 0, "POS has no store theme");
+  assert.deepEqual(failures, [], "no browser console/network failures");
+  console.log(`\n✓ ${viewportCases}/${widths.length * 2 * 2} configured EN/LTR + AR/RTL home/catalogue cases at ${widths.length} widths, ${variants}/${widths.length * 2} variants, 12/12 two-column mobile checks`);
+  console.log(`✓ screenshots: ${output}/ (ignored by Git)`);
+} finally {
+  await browser.close();
+}
